t: This service requires necessarily rectitude and pureness of heart, given by the Blood of Christ. Such rectitude doesn’t come from the adequacy to an external law; it comes from an inner law. And it is only possible to follow the dictates of the inner law if thoroughly docile to the motions of the Holy Spirit.

h: Chapter 1: The spiritual direction in the Revelation
t: Such motion presupposes:

h: A formal disposition, which is the possession of the gifts of the Holy Spirit.
t: A subjective disposition: that is, the election of what is better in each moment and each circumstance.

h: A formal disposition, which is the possession of the gifts of the Holy Spirit.
t: Thus, the Holy Spirit is the true guide and director: When, however, the Spirit comes, who reveals the truth about God; he will lead you into all the truth. (Jn, 16, 13)

h: A formal disposition, which is the possession of the gifts of the Holy Spirit.
t: The Saints understood it in the same way: The principal agent, guide and mover of the souls this business is not the spiritual director, it is the Holy Spirit that never stops caring them”. Many of them experienced it this way: “I have said that Jesus had been ‘my Director’”.
f: Saint John of the Cross, Flame of living love, 3, 46. Saint Teresa of  the Child Jesus, Story of a soul, chapter VII, Complete works, Ed. Monte Carmelo, 1975

h: A formal disposition, which is the possession of the gifts of the Holy Spirit.
t: God is the main author of the straight heart, but He requires, normally, the subsidiary and ministerial help of human direction.

h: A formal disposition, which is the possession of the gifts of the Holy Spirit.
t: The spiritual director is not a Director in a primary and absolute sense, but in a subordinated and relative sense. He must teach the directed person to allow himself be guided by God. Consequently, the main error of the priest is to think that he is the principal Director. The true director of souls, on the contrary:

h: A formal disposition, which is the possession of the gifts of the Holy Spirit.
t: Must feel he is an instrument in the work that God himself makes.

h: A formal disposition, which is the possession of the gifts of the Holy Spirit.
t: Must not impose “a priori” his own points of view.

h: A formal disposition, which is the possession of the gifts of the Holy Spirit.
t: Must have a great prudence, for he doesn’t know, beforehand, God’s plans.

h: A formal disposition, which is the possession of the gifts of the Holy Spirit.
t: He must not form the directed person for him, according to the project he dreams about.

h: Chapter 2:  The spiritual direction in itself.
t: Spiritual direction includes not only the friendly piece of advice and the temporary help the spiritual director can give to anyone who is spiritually needy but also the habitual and complete dedication to the person that seeks the direction as a vital orientation. In other words, it also includes the work of directing, completely applied to the person that submits himself to direction. That is why it is convenient to give different names to the expression “spiritual direction”, according to the different ways in which it is takes place.

h: Chapter 2:  The spiritual direction in itself.
t: Help of direction: when it is given as some friendly advice; it is spiritual but temporary help.

h: Chapter 2:  The spiritual direction in itself.
t: Direction of a person:  even when it is occasional.

h: Chapter 2:  The spiritual direction in itself.
t: Ecclesial ministry of the spiritual direction
We mean, by help of direction, every form of inner and wise cultivation of the disposition of unlimited dedication to the worship given to God.

It is a Christian faithful soul moved by an inner movement of unlimited dedication to the service of God up to the sacrifice of himself. It is a good and righteous man who tries to be still more righteous; it is a man whose will is moved directly to God by a divine motion. Only when this motion moves the whole man with a vital motion, can the man be spiritual and can we speak of a real spiritual direction. Otherwise, it is not but a moral direction.

This means that the directed person devotes himself wholly to God, lets God take him but he also lets man direct and help him. If he doesn’t submit himself spontaneously, spiritual direction can’t take place. It so happens when there isn’t liberality.

Directional help consists in encouraging the soul to grow in a disposition of oblation to God, and in helping the soul to bear the internal difficulties that oppose to God’s guide. If another aim is preferred, spiritual direction spoils, as when for example, it is given primary importance to knowledge based on experience, transforming the spiritual direction in a sort of christian gnosis. In the same way, spiritual direction spoils when it becomes to consist in certain readings, prayers or ascetic practices. These elements must be integrated harmoniously in the spiritual life of each directed person.

The field to cultivate is the inner life. It consists in a work on the inner life spontaneously open. Spiritual direction seeks to help the conscience itself. It is the eye of the spiritual life. As a servant depends on his master … so we will keep looking to you, O Lord our God (Ps. 123, 2) The eyes are like a lamp for the body. If your eyes are sound, your whole body will be full of  light, but if your eyes are not good, your body will be in darkness (Mt. 6, 22-23) *88
f: See also Ef. 4, 17-19

t: There may be in the inner man, certain blindness or deforming illusions. That is why it is necessary to form a sane conscious illuminated by the faith, which reflect the authentic judgments of God, so different from human judgments. It is necessary to form the conscience and lighten the moral judgment.  A conscience that is well formed is upright and truthful. It formulates its judgments according to the reason in conformity to the true good wished by the Wisdom of the Creator.
f: Catechism of the Catholic Church, 1783. "Conscience must be informed and moral judgment enlightened. A well-formed conscience is upright and truthful. It formulates its judgments according to reason, in conformity with the true good willed by the wisdom of the Creator. The education of conscience is indispensable for human beings who are subjected to negative influences and tempted by sin to prefer their own judgment and to reject authoritative teachings. "

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: In this type of spiritual direction, the director is a person who exercises the direction with a certain official acknowledgement of the Church, and the directed person is a Christian faithful who presents himself to the director asking him if he is willing to take charge, during certain time, of his spiritual life. It consists in a periodical contact through which the faithful person lets himself be guided by the director.

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: It is a sort of agreement by which:

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: The directed person opens his heart in order to be directed sincerely.

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: The director guides the director with seriousness along the way of Christian perfection.

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: The Catechism of the Catholic Church reminds that in the formation of the conscience of its members it is necessary the testimony and the advice of others.
f: Ibidem, 1785 "In the formation of conscience the Word of God is the light for our path,[Cf. Ps 119:105 .] we must assimilate it in faith and prayer and put it into practice. We must also examine our conscience before the Lord's Cross. We are assisted by the gifts of the Holy Spirit, aided by the witness or advice of others and guided by the authoritative teaching of the Church.[Cf. DH 14.] "

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: The director, by his very nature, can not give orders. He only advises, but with authority (he requires true obedience, although without obligation under sin).

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: Direction must be wise. Instruction is not enough. Direction must be lead as by osmosis, due to an affective and personal nearness. The director must be a true teacher who possess wisdom, not mere science.

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: It will never be insisted enough on the danger of deformations that can appear in spiritual direction. Spiritual direction may be vitiated:

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: By the spirit of domination (when the director imposes his elections or suffocates the responsibility of the directed person. It is even more dangerous in the direction to women: “I’d like that you do this …”)

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: When the director advices something according to his preference, independently from God’s will.

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: By the director’s vanity, that may vitiate the efficacy.

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: By human uncontrolled affections (some kinds of friendships too human that may lead to jealousy, susceptibility, etc. In these cases the Gospel They are blind leaders of the blind Mt. 15,14)

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: The Church has received from God the task of leading each one of her faithful to the perfection they can reach. In the Church, from the beginning, diverse ministries have taken place in order that her faithful reach such perfection. One of them is the ministry of direction, by which the Church entrusts one of her members -ordinarily the priest- the mission of educating that she has received from Christ, in her personal-and–wise function in order to exercise it on certain communities of members: Major and Minor  Seminaries, Novitiates, Communities of Sisters, Association of laymen, etc
f: See 1 Cor 12, 5.

h: Article 2:  The ministry of direction in the Church.
t: The ecclesiastical ministry of direction embraces the whole spiritual education, in all its aspects. Jesus Christ didn’t want us to stay orphans. Hence, the maternal solicitude of the Church which she exercises through the spiritual direction of her ministers.
f: See Jn 14, 18

h: Article 3: Need to submit oneself to direction
t: Spiritual direction is not absolutely necessary but normally necessary in order reach perfection. It cannot be done without arbitrarily temerity.

h: Article 3: Need to submit oneself to direction
t: Saint Paul himself, after his conversion, in his way to Damascus, was commended to a guide, (Anniah) by Christ Himself.
f: See Ac 9, 6

h: Article 3: Need to submit oneself to direction
t: On the other hand, it is the advice of numerous saints. For example, Saint Bernard: “That who made himself a teacher and a director of himself, would become a disciple of a fool … I  don’t know what others may think of this, but as regards myself, I can say that, according to my experience, it is much easier to direct to  many others than only to myself”. Or also Saint Vincent Ferrer: "Never will Christ give his grace, without which we can do nothing, to anyone that having a virtuous man at his disposal ready to teach and direct him, disregards this help, convinced that he will suffice himself and that he will find by himself what is useful for his salvation”.  On the contrary, “who had a director, to whom he would obey openly and in all, will reach salvation more easily and sooner than by himself, even if we were a man of alive cleverness and had at hand wise books about spiritual matters”
f: Epist. 87,7 De Vita Sspiritualii, p. II, c. 1 Ibid.

h: Article 3: Need to submit oneself to direction
t: 32 Spiritual direction is necessary even nowadays. John Paul II reminds it: “In one’s own life obscurities and even weakness are present. It is the moment of the personal spiritual direction. If one speaks confidently, if one’s own personal inner struggles are exposed with simplicity, one can always succeed, and there will not be any obstacles or temptations that may separate one from Christ”
f: Letter to the seminarians of Spain, Valencia 8/XI/82

h: Chapter 3: The formation of the spiritual director in itself.
t: The qualities of the spiritual director.

h: Chapter 3: The formation of the spiritual director in itself.
t: The spiritual director must be, above all, a father. And to fulfill the obligations of a good father, it is necessary that the director be full of charity. Such charity becomes apparent in the goodness to receive everybody, without favoritism, in his capacity of listening with patience and gentleness, and in the kindness in scolding without disturbing, in other words, in paternal love.

As Saint Francis of Sales states well, the director “must be full of charity, science and prudence. If he lacked any of these virtues, there will be danger in the direction”.  Apart from charity, the queen of the virtues, the director must have some specific qualities inherent to the spiritual direction. Saint Teresa of Jesus has pointed out with precision the technical qualities that a good director must have. He must be wise, discreet and experienced. She says: “it is very important that the teacher be prudent, I mean of good understanding, and have experience, if he is also learned, the business is greatest” .
f: Introduction to the Devout Life, p. I, c. IV Life, 13, 16, see 5, 3; 13, 14; 25, 15;; Way, c. 5

t: Similarly, Saint John of the Cross: “It should be noted that on this way, at least on the highest part of it, and even on  the medium part of it, it will be difficult to find the honorable man that each of the stretches requires,  because apart from being learned, he must be experienced”
f: Flame, c.3, n.30

t: First quality: science: The science of the director must as wide as his duty requires. Apart from a deep knowledge of the dogmatic theology –without which he exposes himself to fail in the faith itself when he gives his judgment about an supernatural phenomenon, and of the moral theology, without which he will not be able to exercise conveniently the duty of simply confessor, he must know spiritual theology very well: what perfection consists in, who and in what manner it binds, which obstacles must be removed, and which positive elements are necessary to be livened. He must know particularly all that regards the life of praying. The different types and grades, the tests that God usually sends or allows in the souls that lead a life of praying (aridity, diabolic assaults, nights of the senses, of the spirit), the difference between first movements, temptations, imperfections and sins properly said, between “feeling” and “consenting”, etc.

The director must also procure to know the basic principles of the human psychology: the theory of the different tempers and characters, the influence that the environment in which the directed person has lived may have had on him, the education he has received. It is also convenient that he know the abnormal cases, that is, the mental and nervous illnesses more frequent.

For this purpose it seems convenient to improve the knowledge, during the studying period, about psychology of the personality and the psychological problems more usual that the priest may find during the administration of the confession and of the spiritual direction. Also, such subjects must be an essential part in the permanent formation of the priests. A means for this may be the monthly meeting for the permanent formation, where this point might be dealt.

Second quality: discretion of spirit.  It is fundamental that the director have  discretion of spirits, that is clarity and penetration  in the judgment to distinguish, in each case, what is true from what is false, what is straight  from what is twisty,  what is healthy  from what is harmful. It is one of the most important qualities that a priest must have. This quality implies prudence in the decisions, clarity in the advice and energy to demand its fulfillment.

It is necessary, thus, that he have a thorough  knowledge of the rules of discernment of spirits, to form and enlighten the consciences of the directed persons, and in an especial way, for the cases in which it is his responsibility to direct souls where extraordinary phenomena appear or gratis mercies are given.
f: Particularly, the two series of rules, for the first and for the second week, that Saint Ignatius gives en his Book of Exercises. See EE, (313-336)

t: Experience. The third quality that the director must have is experience. This experience is gained through the contact with the souls. Being many and so different the ways along which the Holy Sprit leads the souls to the top of sanctity, it is important to compare the own experience with the experience of many other souls, in order to learn how to respect in each soul, the particular way along which God may will to conduct it. The director who would pretend to guide all the souls along the same way and impose indistinctively  his own points of view, never mind how good and excellent they may be, would commit gravest imprudence. It should never be forgotten that the true director is the Holy Spirit, and that the mission of the priest it to  second  his divine Grace, putting apart the obstacles that appear on the way,  and leading the soul to a fidelity each time more exquisite to the inner motions of the grace.
The experience is also reached through the contact with the saints by reading their books and spiritual treaties, attentive to their warnings and advices for the inner life.

But it will also be ideal that the director have personal experience in  spiritual matters, that he himself walk along the way of the virtues that he is called to walk, that he seek God’s will with intensity and that he have a clear discernment  of spirit.

Science tied to discernment  and to  experience is what allows the director to know the directed person well and understand deeply his difficulties: the dumb person (for whom it is difficult to speak) the contradictory person, the obstinate person, the deaf person (the one who doesn’t want to listen), the scrupulous person, the person who thinks about something over and over (that is the person who never goes to the point), the person who seeks to be understood (and consequently is looking for another director),  the one that “supposes that the director supposes”,  the one that brings the problem “solved”,  the one that reasons everything out based on a psychological or human point of view,  the person who pretends to direct the director, the one who wants to kill the time,  the ”hummingbird” (that is the person who is not constant or is superficial), the pessimist person (that sees everything black) , the one “who twists the snake”.
The spiritual director must also have some moral qualities which, not being absolutely necessary for the direction; contribute a lot to its complement and its perfection. Among them we can mention:

A strong piety that is intimacy and life of praying. A great zeal for the sanctification of the souls, following Saint Paul’s example , whose zeal moved  him to become all things to all men in order to win them.
f: See1 Co 9, 22

t: Kindness and delicateness in the character, following the example of Jesus himself that never broke off a bent reed nor put out a flickering lamp and received everybody with immense kindness and compassion. It should not be forgotten that, as San Francis Sales said, “that one can catch more flies with a spoonful of honey than with a hundred barrels of vinegar” *104
f: See Mt 12, 20

t: Disinterestedness and indifference in the dealing with the souls, bearing in mind that those who lead Christ’s sheep as their own, show that they are lovers of their own selves and not of Christ”.  Other directors should never be considered as rivals or competitors in a mission in which nobody may have the pretension of having a monopoly or exclusivity. He must respect the freedom of the souls, loving them, as Saint Paul said, “with a love that comes from the heart of Jesus Christ  himself”
f: Saint Augustine, Tract 123 in Io. See Phil 1, 8

t: In order to carry out the meeting of direction along the spiritual life of the directed person, it is necessary that the director have other qualities such as:
A cordial and sane affection with those who approach him seeking help.
The talent for understanding people.
The art of suggesting with simplicity and efficacy.
Magnanimity and confidence in any enterprise.
The patience of an artist.
The wisdom to distinguish and no to confound points:  the spiritual aspect with the moral or the psychological aspect, the relation as a friend with the relation as a superior.

The direction of others' lives with his own life, giving a continuous example and searching out propitious  opportunities (as excursions, meals,  comments of actuality) for the fruitful dialogue with the directed persons.
The capacity of listening and expressing love and confidence towards his spiritual sons.
Respect to the directed person, without using him and forcing him, without demagogy and simulation in his attitudes and advice.

In other words, the director must seek to grow in the knowledge and love to the souls entrusted to him and in the perfect exercise of the spiritual paternity. To love the souls very much is the secret to help them. Every priest should remember that what he can do in the spiritual direction –as well as during the confession- can’t be done by any other person. Thus, he should always be ready to accept this exercise of pastoral charity.
The concrete realization of the spiritual direction must be understood as a meeting of direction:
A meeting, because it must be a lively moment of cordial and simple dialogue.
Of direction, because the central point of the meeting is the ministry of direction.

It is a pity to see that spiritual direction is distorted frequently in different ways: when it becomes something artificial, when it is merely formal or nominal, when it diverts to secondary subjects or remains on a superficial level instead of getting to the point.
Christ’s example is different: Let’s consider it, for example, the meeting with the disciples of Emmaus
We can see Christ’s intuition, his cordial affection, his confident approach, his invitation to the disciples to open the heart and present the difficulties (vv.15-17)
We can see the disciple’s freedom to present their difficulties without any formalism. (vv.18-24)

Christ listens without taking part; he lets them set free what they have inside. Once they have given vent to their feelings Christ begins to speak spontaneously, he plays “the hard" but lovingly.  He enunciates the truth. He wakes the truth up in the heart of those who already knew it, but had forgotten it (vv 25-27)
Affective adhesion of the disciples, which conscious or unconscious, is adhesion to Christ himself. (v 29)
The human visibility of  the director disappears in order to set the pace to  faith, to Christ invisibly present (vv 30-31)

Enthusiastic conversion of the heart to the community, of those who were already leaving, a singular charismatic effect of inner fervor … and Christ had given no particular orders. He had simply wakened up, in the heart, the spontaneous desire of what He wanted to obtain. (vv 32-24)

Direction must no be carried out in a negative sense, the director contenting himself with listening and correcting some defect, but, and above all, it must focused positively pointing to the acquisition of virtues, guiding, advising and encouraging great enterprises. The director has to, at the same time, remember that the directed person must live by himself, he must bear in mind that he fulfills the function of “crutches”   not of “a wheel chair”.

Directors should try to teach promptly to the souls that seek direction, to do it with the best order and possible fruitfulness, without losing time or without any useless digressions. For this, it is very helpful to bear in mind the aspects that should be dealt during the direction.

Spiritual life (particular examination, sacraments, prayers and penance, practice of the charity). In this area it is important to educate the directed person about how to confess: to distinguish imperfections and temptations. The director should also warn about the importance of not to confess “a list of venial sins” without any intention of emending them, he should recommend the usefulness of associating the confession with the particular exam.
The duties inherent to each state.
The doctrinal and spiritual formation (spiritual readings, studying of  the Christian doctrine)
The apostolate  (discernment to discover God’s will, rectitude of intention, selection and  arrangement of activities according to its importance)

All member of the Institute, aware that the most difficult knowledge and which one avoids most, is the knowledge of oneself., should have a director and rely that, thanks to the spiritual direction he will be helped in the search of Christian perfection. God gives his grace to the person who uses the ordinary means for sanctity.

It is vividly recommended to the members of the Institute the spiritual direction by priests of the same Institute, without detriment of the freedom that the Code of Canonical Law confers. The advantages that follow are many, among them: the specific help in the search of the perfection of the own state, according to the charisma and the aims of the Institute, the help in the conservation and the cultivation of the spirit of the founder, the possession of “a same thought and feeling"

In conformity with the Code of Canonical Law, those who are the very superiors of a house cannot assume the direction of the souls that are under his own responsibility. This gives them more freedom in their functions and in their duty of helping and correcting the religious in the disciplinary and external jurisdiction.

All the priests of our Institute are qualified for the task of spiritual direction. That is why, they must never let themselves be intimidated by a false humility, scruples or shyness. Bearing this in mind, the older priest should encourage and drive the younger priests to the exercise of direction.

A priest of our Institute must never think or feel himself the owner of the souls, not even give the impression that he has some power on the souls, or that he is zealous by the fact that others exercise direction. Furthermore, he must know how to lead the souls to other priests when necessary and be careful that the souls do not feel disorderly affection to his own person.

Every priest that foresees being moved to other destination should, with enough time, advice the souls that are being directed by him, in the election of a new director. He should avoid, by reason of natural modesty or any other reason, any delay which would leave the souls without a director for some time.
The members of the Institute should bear in mind that the direction and confession of the members among themselves is an excellent expression of delicate charity that must reign in the community.

In the houses of formation there must be priests that have enough time and, if possible, be free of duties not pertaining to those houses, in order to attend the requirements of spiritual direction. Students should consider that they are strongly recommended to choose as their spiritual fathers, the spiritual directors assigned there.  Nevertheless, the freedom that the Code of Canonic Law gives, to chose another priest, will always be present

Every priest of the Institute should have, as an absolute priority in his apostolate the attention and availability   towards his brethren in his religious life. That is why, to encourage the visits, especially to those who are far away and isolated is one of the clearest expressions of exquisite charity.
All the houses should have times and places for the practice of the direction and the confession, such as:
The diary time for the Adoration of the Blessed Sacrament.
The weekly penitential Liturgy
The monthly retires.

The secret the subjects of the spiritual direction, must be observed strictly both by the director as well as by the directed person. The superiors or any other persons must keep even the appearance that they might wish to know any subjects of the spiritual direction.
f: CIC, c. 220

t: The spiritual directors must be warned about some aberrations that may occur during the spiritual direction, such us
Their interference in the external jurisdiction of the government of the houses of the Institute
Their taking part of the play of those who want to use the direction for other purposes.

Their taking part of part of the play of those who change their directors easily, arguing false dialectical reasons. Therefore, directors should require from the directed person, enough reasons of spiritual benefit, in order to accept a change.

In the houses of formation, the spiritual directors should procure to get, from the superiors, all information about the progress of their directed persons, having in mind a more efficacious direction.  The superiors, should, at the same time, be informed about the frequent practice of the spiritual direction to the students.  It is convenient that the superior of a house should know who the director of each person that is being formed is, and that he should inform the director about the news that has happened in the external jurisdiction which may help the director in his task.

In other houses of the Institute, it seems convenient, when and if the Superior considers it opportune, if the Superior asks the director about it, that the director say to him, if the directed persons practice or not the direction. This may be useful specially to help to correct –paternally or fraternally, a certain member of the Institute.
Obviously, many of the points considered above, are totally valid in the area of the apostolic activity, especially those referred to the spiritual direction.
As regards the time, the places and the means for the exercise of spiritual direction, it is recommended:
The festive oratory for children and young people.
The Holy Hour established in the Parishes, Schools, Hospitals, etc.
The monthly retire of perseverance for laymen.

It seems very convenient that the priests predicate about the marvelous benefits of the spiritual direction and of the frequent confession. They should insist, at the same time, to the persons that do spiritual exercises according to the method of Saint Ignatius, that they should incorporate the habitual spiritual direction in the reform of life.

The priests must be convinced that it is in the personal dealing with the souls that takes place during the spiritual direction where the fruits of sanctity most pleasant to God are cultivated, and that it is there where the soul is helped to discern all types of motions or initiatives to discover God’s will on it.

In the exercise of spiritual direction, the reasons and criteria to correct, discern, suggest or incite must always be supernatural. The director should be especially on guard against the prudence of the flesh.

Finally, our priests and the whole Institute, should be known for the frequent pastoral practice of the confession and of the spiritual direction. People should know that everywhere they find a priest of our religious family, they will always find a spiritual father.

h: Chapter 1: Education of the Christian attitudes.
t: Spiritual direction aims to form Christian people that grow to the perfection of Jesus’ measure. There is one thing that is clear and cannot be replaced:  it is the love to Christ what should be the principal thing for the directed person, a true falling in love with Christ. Beside Him, the Virgin and the Saints will occupy an important place. There should be flexibility in the rest. Thus, it should be procured that the director adapt himself  to each directed person, according to the individual differences of each man, of one time and another, of the characters, and of the graces that God distributes.

h: Chapter 1: Education of the Christian attitudes.
t: It is convenient to warn the directed about the temptation, especially in the beginning, of feeling an apparent hypocrisy in the practice of the direction, that he may have the impression of certain artificiality in his conduct.  It must be taught that sincerity is not the adequacy between what is felt and what is expressed but between personal conviction and its expression. If any feelings that do not correspond to our personal conviction, should arise, they should be considered as "alien parasites"

h: Chapter 1: Education of the Christian attitudes.
t: That is why, it must be sought that the activities of the directed persons should be, each time, further inmost. Spiritual activities have an efficacy of disposition, of physical not sacramental efficiency. They are instrumental, they are not principal they do not depend on the material execution of certain acts. Their doing must be

h: Chapter 1: Education of the Christian attitudes.
t: In spirit: they should not end in external action though they may use them as a means.

h: Chapter 1: Education of the Christian attitudes.
t: Cordial:  the whole heart must take part of them.

h: Chapter 1: Education of the Christian attitudes.
t: Total: they should transform the whole man and all his manifestations.

h: Chapter 1: Education of the Christian attitudes.
t: Spiritual direction must aim to form the person giving unity to the spiritual life.  Sometimes one falls in the error of thinking that spiritual life occupies only a part of the life of man. On the contrary, the whole life must be spiritual and supernatural. Human being reaches this unification of his life by three fundamental attitudes:  prayer (that gives him his vertical dimension and makes him “belong to God”), abnegation (that makes him, in a sense, not to belong to himself; it is the area of Christian abnegation, of external and inner renounce; it has its strong moment in God) and the active service to the brothers (that makes him belong to the others)
f: See LG, c. 5, n. 42

h: Chapter 1: Education of the Christian attitudes.
t: It must, at the same time seek to form a praying attitude. Spiritual direction must have as an objective to make the directed person reach a life of praying, that is, to make him live in the presence of God, and that his whole life be a living in a prayer of petition, in a state of immersion in God. The object of spiritual direction is not but to elevate the spiritual life, the life of union with God.

h: Chapter 1: Education of the Christian attitudes.
t: It must seek, also, to form the person in the abnegation and mortification. The director must explain, for this reason, the evangelic concept of abnegation, and initiate the directed person  into the meaning of the Cross, until the directed person reach “the wisdom of the Cross”,  such as the great saints understood it, as Saint John of the Cross and Saint Louis Maria Grignion de Montfort.

h: Chapter 1: Education of the Christian attitudes.
t: Finally, spiritual direction must have the goal of forming the directed person in the edification of the Church. The director must never lose sight of the fact that the sanctification always takes place in the Church and when the benefit of the Church is sought. The directed person is not an isolated soul but he belongs to a concrete ecclesial community, and is part of the mystic body of Christ. For that reason, direction will point to form in the directed person, the apostolic and missionary dimension, living up the illusions of taking the gospel to all the peoples, so that all the people believe in Christ.
f: For technical reasons, the modes corresponding to paragraphs 77-80 elaborated by the Capitulary Fathers, were lost. The ones that are presented here correspond to the same content, but as their actual redaction was not submitted to vote, they are introduced ad referendum of the next General Chapter

h: Chapter 2: The discernment of spirit as the objective of the spiritual direction.
t: The progress in the spiritual life is manifested in a fidelity each time greater to God’s consent to man, not only in what refers to the election of the state of life once, but also in all particular cases, in such a way that the Christian faithful may understand God’s will in the different moments and may begin to set his hand to it with diligence. One of the aspects that spiritual direction must develop in the directed person is the exercise of distinguishing “God’s signs”, now objective (the signs of the times), then subjective (inner motions).

h: Chapter 2: The discernment of spirit as the objective of the spiritual direction.
t: Spiritual direction must initiate the directed person in the “discernment of spirits”, in other words, help the directed person to be conscious of how, during the development of the inner life, certain states of mind, inclinations, wishes, projects, temptations will arise. The director must orientate the directed person indicating the possible origin of these phenomena, giving concrete and precise norms which may help him to discern and act in each case.
f: It will be very useful for this purpose, to recommend to the directed person, the practice of the spiritual exercises according to Saint Ignatius’ method.

h: Chapter 2: The discernment of spirit as the objective of the spiritual direction.
t: At the same time, the director will help the directed person in the discernment in the moments of special difficulty in the spiritual life. He will have to attend and purify all that refers to the vocation and to the special charismas, detect possible spiritual illusions and help un the crisis proper to growth, now personal, then apostolic.

h: Chapter 3: Attention in cases of illnesses of the soul
t: As a “doctor of souls”, the director must know how to distinguish certain illnesses of the soul:

h: Chapter 3: Attention in cases of illnesses of the soul
t: Illnesses totally spiritual, such as spiritual mediocrity or coolness.

h: Chapter 3: Attention in cases of illnesses of the soul
t: Illnesses with a physiological base, such as depressions, irascibility, spiritual apathy, etc.

h: Chapter 3: Attention in cases of illnesses of the soul
t: Spiritual illnesses with psychological effects, especially perplexity of conscience in what refers to chastity and scruples.

1.The popular missions, or missions to the people, are known by many different names such as: Popular Missions; Missions to the town; Missions to the faithful; Holy Missions; “ad intra” Missions; Sacred Missions;Traditional Missions; Missions to the Catholics; Missions to the interior or Internal Missions, etc.
f: Cf. CIC, c. 770.

t: It is a popular and simple form of preaching The Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ to the whole Town of God. It is the fulfillment of Christ’s missionary mandate: “Go into the whole world and proclaim the Gospel to every creature. Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved; whoever does not believe will be condemned (Mk 16:15-16).
The missionary prolongs Jesus Christ’s work who began to preach and to say: "Repent, because the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand" (Mt 4:17).

The end of popular Missions follows the missionary mandate and is very well expressed by Saint Louis Marie Grignion de Montfort: "renewal of Christianity in believers”; and by Saint Alphonsus Maria of Liguori: “the end of the missions (is) the conversion of sinners.” His Holiness John Paul II teaches that the popular Mission “is effective when…it impels to conversion, that is to say, the return to the truth and to God’s friendship of those who have lost their faith and grace because of sin; it calls routine Christians to a more perfect life, it gives fervor to souls, it convinces people to live the beatitudes, and it draws priestly and religious vocations.”
f: Rules to the missionary priests, nº 56,  B.A.C., Madrid, 1984,  p. 583. Letter to a new bishop , ascetic works, B.A.C., Madrid, 1954,  p. 380. Juan Pablo II The announcement of the Gospel in the modern society, speech to the participants of the national Italian congress about “Missions to the town for the 80`s, (06/02/1981); or (08/03/1981), p.2.

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: The analogous principle of the missions is the missions ‘ad gentes.’ For all of them it is indispensable to be familiar with Pope John Paul II’s encyclical, “Redemptoris missio.”

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: The missionary duty is “unique and identical in all parts of the world and in any circumstance, though it is not practised identically due to the fact that it depends on particular instances. The differences are not based on intrinsic reasons of the mission itself, but on the diverse situations in which it is developed.”
f: RMs, 33.

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: Its ultimate principle is found in the “ad intra” Trinitarian processions and the “ad extra” missions. There are two “ad intra” processions: the generation of the Son and the expiration of the Holy Spirit. God is an intelligent being; the object of his understanding is his own essence: He understands himself. The concept that God eternally forms of himself is the Word. Between the Father and the Son they exhale the Holy Spirit through love.

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: The temporary missions, or “ad extra” missions, include the eternal processions and they add a new manner of presence:

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: - First, the sending of his Son, Supreme and Eternal Missionary: "God sent his Son" (Gal 4:4).

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: - Secondly, the sending of the Holy Ghost: “God sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts” (Gal 4:6).

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: The temporary missions, or “ad extra” missions, can be visible or invisible.

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: There are two visible missions:

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: -The Incarnation, which is a substantial mission: “The Word became flesh...” (Jn 1:14);

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: -and the descent of the Holy Ghost at Pentecost, which is a representative mission: “then there appeared to them tongues as of fire, which parted and came to rest on each one of them” (Act 2:3).

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: And throughout the history of the Church, the invisible, temporal mission is the Trinitarian indwelling of sanctifying grace in the soul of the faithful, because the three Persons come to dwell in the soul: In this we know that we remain in Him  and He in us: “He has given us his Spirit” (Jn 4:13); “Whoever loves me will keep my word, and my Father will  love him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him” (Jn 14:23).

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: The popular mission seeks to communicate to people the invisible “ad extra” mission: that the Trinity dwells within souls by grace.

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: A principle that should govern the whole missionary activity of our Institute,  because it is the revelation of the salvific will of God, is the rule that Saint Paul  formulated  to his disciple, Timothy, bishop and missionary: “God wants all men to be saved and to reach the full knowledge of the truth” (1Tim 2:4).

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: Therefore, all those who truly love God know that He has not predestined anyone to eternal condemnation, and because of this, they make use of all ordinary and extraordinary means in order to reach every man’s salvation through Jesus Christ, the only Savior, and to be able to say together with Blessed Louis Orione: "Lord, place me at the mouth of hell, so I, through your mercy, may seal it.“
f: Notes of February, 1939, quoted in  On way with Orione,  Ed. Pcia. Our Lord of  theGuard, Argentina,T.III, p. 427;Const. (356).

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: Conscious that “there is no salvation through anyone else, nor there is any other name under heaven given to the human race by which we are to be saved” (Act 4:12), the missionaries of the Institute understand,  together with the Tradition and the perennial Magisterium,  that “there is no salvation outside the Church,” because “the Church is the same  Christ who lives among us...; it is the mysterious dwelling of Jesus Christ with us; it is another Christ,” and it is only in Jesus Christ, and under the action of the Holy Spirit, that men can enter into communion with God: “No one comes to the Father except through me” (Jn 14:6).  As John Paul II expresses:  “This unique and
f: Cf. Dz. 1473; Lg, 14; Catechism of the Catholic Church, 846; cf.  1257, 1129. Mons.Tihamer Toth,  I  believe in the Church, Society of Education “Atenas”, S.A., Madrid, pp. 47-48.

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: universal mediation, far from being an obstacle on the walk towards God, is the way established by God Himself, and of which Christ has full consciousness."
f: RM, 5.

h: Article 4: The Missions and the Holy Trinity
t: There are diverse ways to belong to Christ's Church. In whichever manner, salvation comes only through Jesus Christ. Our mission is to make it so that all men be members of the Church “in act,” as it is clearly evident that salvation is offered to all men: "Christ died for all, and man's supreme vocation is only one, that is to say, divine. In consequence, we should believe that the Holy Spirit offers to all men the possibility, in a form only known to God, of being associated to this paschal mystery."

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: Our way of viewing the paradigm of all missions is that of the first mission of the disciples narrated by Saint Luke, chapter 10.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: ... The Lord appointed 72 others... (v 1). God is the one who designates and chooses His missionaries. As He did before with the 72 disciples, He continues to do so now through His Church. Bishops and religious superiors choose missionaries in His name and with His authority.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: ...and He sent them... (v 1). God not only chooses, but also sends. This sending resembles the sending of the Son : “As the Father has sent me, so I send  you” (Jn 20:21). It is this sending which formally constitutes the mission.
f: Mission: fron the Latin term  meo, as, are  (at the same time from Greek uevo = go, and from  avjmeno = to pass ) , so,  mitto, is, missi, missum, ere, a (freq. From meo ) = to pass from one place to another one, the spanish word mision comes from there, according to the Dictionary of the Real Spanish Academy, it means: “1- The act of sending. 2. The power, the ability that one gives to a person to carry out a  duty  3-duty. 4-Pilgrimage that the religious and apostolic men make from town to town...preaching the Gospel. 5-Series or group of fervent sermons that the missionaries and apostolic men preach during the evangelical pilgrimages. 6 - House or Church of the missionaries...7-Earth, county or place where the missionaries preach. Dictionary of the Spanish Language,  21ª edition,  Madrid, 1992,  p.977.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: … in pairs... (v 1). Our Lord had His reasons to act in this way and, in fact, many people continue proceeding in the same way. Saint  Gregory the Great said: "He sent them in this way  because there are two precepts of charity: love of God and love of neighbor; and there cannot be charity with less than two: this shows that whoever has no charity with his brothers, should not take the responsibility of preacher."  Our Constitutions say: "it is a fact that in mathematics one plus one is two, but one man plus another man are two thousand men. A man together with another grows in courage and strength, fear disappears, and he can escape from any trap."
f: Homily 17, in Evang. Const. (402).

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: ...ahead of him... (v 1). Christ sends His missionaries so that they would prepare the road by which He Himself would come to souls. This is the great consolation of the authentic missionary, the certainty of being sent by Whom and for Whom it is that comes to men. The missionary is a precursor, like Saint John the Baptist, who proclaims with his words and actions: "... A Man is coming after me" (Jn 1:30). From this comes the unyielding confidence in the inexhaustible power of the mission to bring about the conversion of men.  It is Jesus Christ Himself who wants to come to them.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: ... to every town and place... (v 1). There is no place where a soul is that is prohibited to the missionary. The missionary should go to the most humble houses, to the highest of high places, to the most rugged and rough places, where there are less people, where they expect less fruits, where the people are most unruly, where there are the most difficulties...there, the missionary should go taking his own staff, by automobile, plane, on foot or horse, sulky or ship...because this  is his vocation, and to this obedience sends him.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: ... where He intended to go (v 1). We are His ambassadors:  We are, then, ambassadors of Christ, as if God appealed through us (2 Cor 5:20). Our mission is to bring Christ: "There is no true evangelization, if the name, the doctrine, the life, the promises, the Kingdom, the mystery of Jesus of Nazareth, Son of God are not announced."
f: EN, 22

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: ...And He said to them: “The harvest is abundant but the laborers are few; so, ask the master of the harvest  to send out laborers for his harvest" (v 2). The apostolic work is enormous; we have to cover our ears when someone contradicts the words of the Lord, saying that there are many vocations. The laborers will always be few and the harvest will always be abundant. Only “thieves and robbers,” only a “mercenary” pastor can be so criminal as deflecting, discouraging, not working for, or being against vocations, because he does the work of a thief who comes to steal, to kill and to destroy... who leaves the sheep and runs away." It is always necessary to pray to God asking for workers for His harvest; and one of the great fruits of the popular Missions is vocations to consecrated life.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: Go on your way, behold, I am sending you like lambs among wolves (v 3). Our Lord insists: Go..., alerting us of the dangers that we will face. We are defenseless prophets, we only have spiritual weapons: Put on the armor of God so that you may be able to stand firm against the tactics of the devil. For our struggle is not with flesh and blood but with the principalities, with the powers, with the world rulers of this present darkness, with the evil spirits in the heavens. Therefore, put on the armor of God, that you may be able to resist on the evil day and, having done everything, to  hold on your ground. So stand fast with your loins girded in truth, clothed with righteousness as a breastplate, and your feet shod in readiness for the gospel of peace. In all circumstances, hold faith as a shield, to quench all the flaming arrows of the evil one. And take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the spirit, which is the word of God. With all prayer and supplication, pray at every opportunity in the Spirit. To that end, be watchful with all perseverance and supplication for all the holy ones ...(Eph 6:11-18). Pastoral work means the cross, difficulties, dangers, sufferings: it means not taking advantage of the milk, meat, or the wool of the sheep, it is necessary to be like Saint Paul: I want not what is yours but you (2 Cor 12:14). Those who evacuate the cross, evacuate the pastoral work. That is why there are so many strident and clamorous pastoral failures. The sheep will not follow a stranger; they will run away from him, because they do not recognize  the voice of  strangers (Jn 10:5).

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: Do carry neither a bag, nor a sack, nor sandals (v 4). It does not mean that our Lord wishes us to lack all goods, but it refers to the spirit of poverty that every missionary should have. They should not be attached to unnecessary things. The complete concern should be for no other than the missionary end. It is necessary to trust limitlessly in Providence, using all means.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: And do not greet anyone along your way (v 4). The task is urgent, there is no time to waste, nor occasions to do good: "the occasion is like iron, it is necessary to strike while its hot." The charity of Christ impels us (2 Cor 5:14).

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: Into whatever house you enter, first say: " Peace to this house" (v 5). It is necessary to go where people live, to their environment, where they work. Nowadays, asking people to come to the Temple is not enough. It is necessary to go and meet the people! The first sermon of the Mission is usually about peace, because the peace of Christ is the purpose of the popular mission. The great work of the popular Mission is the pacification of souls in order to reconcile them with God.
f: Cf. Junquera, Saturnino S.J., The Holy  Mission, Ed. Sal Terrae, Santander, 1953, p.359 ss.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: If a peaceful person lives there, your peace will rest on him (v 6). Peace is the greeting, the program and the fruit of the popular Missions. That is why personal visits are so important, they aim to place all people into the grace of God, and that is to carry peace. For that reason, it is necessary to guide people's conversation, to avoid being wrapped up in their topics, but pointing to their conversion. If not, (peace) will return to you (v 6). Peace which comes from God can not be without effect, if it does not rest on those visited, it will return to the missionaries who will benefit from it. Those missionaries who wish other people’s peace win merits for themselves.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: Stay in the same house...( v 7). The apostolic visit should not be a “medical visit.” It is necessary to take enough time to be able to detect the spiritual necessities of the family, their difficulties, to be able to carry out a consultation, to answer their doubts, to break their sophisms contrary to the faith, etc.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: It is not advisable to accept, during the Mission, invitations to eat at family houses, because lunches are usually prolonged too much, and this provokes detriment of the Mission, since the necessary hour to rest and the contact with the other missionaries would be left aside. It is preferable that the families, in an organized manner, bring food to where all of the missionaries meet. In a very exceptional situation, it could be acceptable to eat with the families, but after-meal chats must be avoided. We should be disposed to everything, accommodate ourselves to the customs, as the Word surrendered, however, we should not consent to sin.
f: Cf. Phil  2,6

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: ...Because the laborer deserves his salary...Whatever town you enter and they welcome you, eat what is offered to you  (v 7). You should not  reject the alms that they freely offer, moreover, it allows them to make a charitable act, and to help to finance the expenses of the mission. According to our experience each mission is paid by itself. To reject charity could be seen as a neglect and it is necessary to educate for charity.
f: Cf. 2 Cor 8,7.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: Do not move from house to house (v 7). That is to say, in a hurry, as doing a census, but giving more importance to the spiritual fruits of each visit than to the quantity of houses you visit.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: ...Cure the sick in it …(in the city)... (v 9). The physical and material attention of the sick is convenient, but one should not lose sight of the purpose of the visit, transforming it into a social visit.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: ...And say to them: "The Kingdom of God is at hand for you" (v 9). The expression “Kingdom of God” appears 50 times in the Gospels; " Reign of Heavens ” 39 times, it has three meanings:

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: a) It has been prepared with the work of the patriarchs and prophets in the Old Testament and it became present in the Person and work of Christ.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: b) It descends in Pentecost thanks to the Holy Spirit of whom the Catholic Church will be born. It is the earthly phase of the Kingdom, which is universal, spiritual, internal and external (that is to say, social with its sacraments and hierarchy), which does not exclude the bad and their mixture with the good, which has to be discovered, conquered and expanded.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: c) It comes on the day of the Final Judgment, time only known by God and which will take us by surprise (Mk 13:32). It is the celestial phase of the Kingdom.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: In the mission, the Kingdom of God is spoken of in its second meaning: the Church whose Head is Christ, as an external Universal Kingdom (members, temples), and internal (the Grace). This Kingdom should be extended. It is necessary to conquer souls for this Kingdom, and in this way to expand it.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: The popular mission is a pure mission and typically missionary, or rather, ordered for the salvation of souls. It is focused on the   metanoia, that they will repent (Mk 6:12), on the renewal, on the change of “modes of thinking.”

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: Whatever town you enter and they do not receive you, go out into the streets and say: " The dust of your town that clings to our feet, even that, we shake off against you.” Yet know this:  the Kingdom of God is at hand" (v 10,11). The act of shaking the dust in the place, city or house where it proceeds shows that it is profane earth in which one does not want to participate, and in that way, you it gives testimony against them (Mk 6:11). We are also taught, that even in the event of rejection, it is necessary to know how to announce, as far as possible, the Gospel.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom on that day than for that town, woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! Because if the mighty Dees done in your midst had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would long ago have repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes. But it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgement than for you. And as for you, Capernaum, Will you be exalted to heaven? You will go down to the netherworld (v 12:15)! Even the Supreme and Eternal missionary knew the apparent missionary failure. If He knew it, we can also know it:  No disciple is above his teacher, no slave is above his master (Mt 10:24). An apparent missionary failure should not disappoint us, on the contrary, it should revive our apostolic work.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: 34.Whoever listens to you, listens to me; whoever rejects you, rejects me. And whoever rejects me, rejects the one who sent me (v 16). For that reason, it is necessary to have much delicacy in order to avoid being the cause of the rejection. It is necessary to have great kindness of heart and to be clearly conscious that our words should be those of Christ. Who rejects the missionary, rejects Christ and rejects the Father. The good missionary should put into practice the advice that Saint John Marie Vianney gave to a priest who complained about the sterility of his apostolic efforts: "You have raised your prayers to God, cried, sighed, complained; but,  have you fasted, kept vigil slept on the floor and whipped yourself ? While you have not done these, do not believe that you have tried your best.”
f: Secret Vatican file, S.C. from rites, Canonization Process, volume 227, p. 53; quoted by John XXIII, encyclical Sacerdotii nostri primordia, (01/08/1959), nº 42, Colec. Enc. Pont, Ed. Guadalupe, Bs. As., volume II, p. 2339.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: The 72 returned rejoicing... (v 17). Inevitably, the missionary always returns from the mission with an immense happiness. Perhaps, there is no happier man than an authentic missionary, because: Blessed the one who comes in the name of God! (Sal 118:26). Promises made by God will be executed: "Blessed are the peacemakers ..." (Mt 5:9).

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: ...saying: "Lord, even the demons are subject to us because of your name.” He told them: “I have observed Satan fall like lightning from the sky" (v 17-18). That is the effect of a good mission well carried out: the fall of the demon for not being able to capture souls by sin. And that is the motive for the missionary’s happiness, although, there are motives more lofty.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: Behold, I have given to you the power to tread upon serpents and scorpions and upon the full force of the enemy and nothing will  harm you... (v 19). For that reason, not even all of the forces of hell together will have power over the missionary, because to him does receives power from Christ. Nothing can harm the true disciple of the Lord: do not be afraid of those who kill the body, they  can not kill the soul (Mt 10:28).

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: ...Nevertheless,” do not rejoice because the spirits are subject to you; but rejoice because your names are written in heaven”  (v 20). The greatest motive for the missionary’s happiness is to have been chosen by God to preach his Gospel; election and mission which will not be left without recompense: My brothers, if anyone among you should stray from the truth and someone brings him back, he should know that whoever brings back a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins (Jas 5: 19-20).

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: At that very moment He rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I give you praise, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, for although you have hidden these things from the wise and the learned you have revealed them to the childlike. Yes, Father, such has been your gracious will. All things have been handed over to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and who the Father is, except the Son and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal him" (v 21,22). Jesus showed himself inundated with joy, just as the missionary who has finished a Mission feels, because he that principally works during the mission is Jesus. He is always the first Missionary and the first one to be happy. Jesus is filled with our joy, and we should let him inundate us with His joy. These are hidden things to those who consider themselves wise and intelligent, but in fact, are arrogant. Such is the gracious will of the Father. Every Mission originates in the Trinity and terminates in the Trinity, in benefit to those to whom the Son wishes to reveal this.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: Turning to the disciples in private He said :”Blessed are the eyes that see what you see. For I say to you, many prophets and kings desired to see what you see, but did not see it, and to hear what you hear, but did not hear it” (v 23-24). Blessed by experiencing the reality of God’s Kingdom, which is established thanks to the Messiah, Jesus Christ, through whom the Father acts, a thing seen neither by the prophets who announced it  - Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel... - nor by the kings of whom the Messiah would descend: - David, Solomon... - but seen by the missionaries.

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: The text of the Gospel according to Saint Luke finishes with two facts that, for us, manifest the two great foundations of the popular Missions: one is the charity and mercy that the missionary should have. Teacher, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”…"You shall love the Lord, your God, with all your heart, with all your being, with all your strength, and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself " . ... And “Who is my neighbor?" ...He said:  "The one who treated him with mercy" (v 25,29,37).

h: Article 5: The Model of All Popular Missions
t: The other one is prayer. When there is no prayer, there is no charity; and when there is no charity, there is no prayer, and by reason of this lacking, there are not many authentic missionaries... you are anxious and worried about many things; and there is need of only one thing. Mary has chosen the best part and it will not be taken from her (v 41-42).
There are different classes of Popular Missions:
- The most common is the intensive one, which is carried out during ten, fifteen, or more days. In theory, this would be all the days necessary to dispose all to confess.
- The permanent one, which lasts most of the year, especially, the ministry of home visits.
- The youth mission, carried out together with the intensive one or, preferably, in the secondary schools, universities or in any other place of concentration of youth.
- The children’s mission, which is similar to the previous one but is focused on children.
- The mission for the sick, dedicated especially to them.
- The industrial mission, when it is carried out in the industries.
- The open Mission, when it is carried out through any media, especially, the television and the radio.

- The Mission, according to the territory, can be general, (organized in a dioceses), parochial or in buildings of many families, centers for listening to the Word or other variations which are discovered to be convenient.
With much profit there can be, at the same time, different types of popular Missions according to the necessities and, mainly, according to the possibilities.

God willed that the world be saved through missionaries. Throughout time, God sent workers to cultivate his vineyard. In the Old Testament, He sent the patriarchs and prophets; in the New Testament, the Supreme and Eternal Missionary: Jesus Christ, sent by his Father; then, the Apostles and their successors were sent: Go into the whole world and proclaim the Gospel to every creature (Mk 16:15). The whole history of the Church testifies the sending of laborers... that is why the wise father Contenson affirms: "Only through the missions do souls attain their eternal salvation."  For that reason, Saint Alphonsus says: "Clearly seen are the efforts of hell to avoid the missions."
f: Quoted by Saint Alphonsus Marie of Liguori, Ascetic works, Useful reflexions to the bishops, p. 38; cf. Letter to a new bishop, p. 380. Op. quot., p. 38; cf. Letter to a new bishop, p. 380.

t: The importance of preaching and the missions is so great that the Church points out that the priest has “among his main duties, the announcement of the Gospel of God to everybody."  And to the parish priests it prescribes that:  "During certain times...the parish priests should organize those forms of preaching named spiritual exercises and sacred missions or others adapted to these necessities."
f: CIC, c. 762. CIC, c. 770.

t: Likewise, the Third General Latin-American Episcopal Conference in Puebla: “It would go in a simultaneous form to the groups and to the multitudes. For these last ones, the popular Missions have great effectiveness, conveniently renewed in an evangelizing line."
f: Puebla, nº 1010.

t: Convinced of the necessity of the “Missions to the People,” John Paul II repeats untiringly: “Because of this, today I repeat with greater force and conviction what I have already wrote in the Apostolic Letter “Catechesi Tradendae": "The traditional missions are irreplaceable for a periodic and vigorous renovation of Christian life. ”
f: CT, 47. In the same text , the Pope regrets that the popular missions were abandoned in an excessive hurry “so many times”. Ibid, 4.

t: The urgency of preaching has its foundation in Holy Scripture: "When writing to the Romans, Saint Paul highlights: faith is by preaching, by the Word of Christ (1 Co 1:30). Therefore, it is necessary to go, to speak, to preach, to teach, to announce, so that men could believe and invoke."

h: Article 8:  The Popular Missions at Present
t: There have always been people who “dream up vain pretexts to impede the mission in their parishes."  Among them, there are those who affirm that they are not appropriate for our days; that is why John Paul II must remember their perennial presence: "I manifest to you, moreover, my gratitude and that of the whole Church because of  the interest and the good will in maintaining and modernizing the fervor and effective practice of the popular Missions. Remembering what the Divine Teacher commanded: Go and teach to all people..., teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you (Mt 28:19-20), we can do no less than  obey with courage and with joy, announcing to all men that Jesus Christ has come to be for us, on the part of God, wisdom as well as justice, sanctification and redemption (1 Co 1:30).
f: Saint Alphonsus Marie of Liguori, Op.cit.,  p. 382. John Paul II, op.cit., 4.

h: Article 8:  The Popular Missions at Present
t: “Christ's command and the Apostle's severe warning  are still valid. They have been the stimulus which has made the great Fathers intrepid and untiring, the great Saints, to whom it is necessary to make reference constantly if we really want to illuminate and to save our brothers: Ignatious of Loyola, Phelip Neri, Vicent of Paul, Alphonsus Marie of Liguori, Saint Paul of the Cross, Louis Grignion of Monfort, Gaspar of Buffalo, Francis de Sales, John Baptist Vianney, Maximilian Kolbe: brilliant and concrete men who ‘Popular Missions’ of maximum value."
f: Cf. 1 Cor 9,16. John Paul II, op.cit., 4.

t: Renovated Methods and Modernized Criteria

All missionary saints have known how to adapt to the times and diverse necessities of their audience, as Saint Alphonsus M. of Liguori expressly states: "What use is there for the sick to report prescriptions which the doctor has prescribed at random, before knowing their illnesses?”
f: Cf. Infra History of the Popular Missions. Saint Alphonsus Marie of Liguori, Ascetic Works, Useful reflexions to bishops, p. 38; cf. Letter to a new bishop, p. 383.

t: In our days John Paul II insists: "...I exhort all of you to renew them, to revalue them, to propose them again with modernized methods and criteria adapted to the dioceses and to the parishes, in accordance with the local Churches.”
f: John Paul II, op.cit., 4,  Cf. CIC, c. 770.

t: "Today, for an effective work in the area of preaching, it is necessary, before all else, to know very well the spiritual and psychological reality of the Christians who live in the modern society. It is necessary to admit, realistically, and with deep and tormented sensibility that Christians today, for the most part, feel misplaced, confused, perplexed and even disappointed; they have spread before them ideas contrasting the real truth which has been revealed and always taught; ideas that are truly and properly heresies in the dogmatic and moral sphere have been spread, creating doubts, confusions, rebellions, the liturgy has even been manipulated; they are immersed in an intellectual and moral  "relativism," and due to this, in permissive-ism, Christians are tempted by atheism, agnosticism, the vaguely moralistic illuminism, by a sociological Christianity, without defined dogmas and without  an objective  morality. It is necessary to know the man of today in order to be able to understand how to listen to him and to love him as he is, not to excuse the wrong, but to discover his roots, well-convinced that everybody can have salvation and mercy under, the condition of not rejecting them consciously and obstinately.”

“Today, the evangelical figures of the good Samaritan, the father of the prodigal son, the Good Shepherd prove to be particularly present. It is necessary to constantly take the pulse of our time, to be able to know the current man.”
The Pope’s words are very clear if some elements are taken into account:
To illuminate minds and
To encourage maternally.

“For an authentic and effective ‘mission,’ it is necessary to illuminate minds in a complete and sure way. Today, it is not enough to state a concept, it is necessary to listen first, to realize where the other is, in his path of searching or in his drama of defeat or escape, it is necessary to explain things and to be attentive to the other’s demands.”

To encourage maternally: “Today, it is necessary to be patient and to begin again from the beginning, from the “preambles of the faith” up to the “novisimos,” with clear, documented and satisfactory exposition. It is necessary to form the intelligence with illuminated and strong convictions, because it is the only way to form consciences. Today, above all it is necessary to capture and to inculcate the “sense of mystery,” the necessity of humility of reason when facing the Infinite and the Absolute, the logic of confidence and trust in Christ and the Church, which is loved and founded by Him to always give men the peace of truth and the happiness of grace. It is a delicate and even tiring task which demands careful preparation and psychological sensibility; however, it is absolutely necessary.”
f: John Paul II, op. cit.,  4; CIC, c. 770.

t: Not only that but also “…it is necessary to encourage people maternally with the same love as Christ. The “popular Mission” is effective when, accompanied by prayer and penance, it impels to conversion, that is to say, the return to the truth and friendship of God for those who had lost their faith and grace because of sin, it calls routine Christians to a more perfect life, it gives fervor to souls, it convinces people to live the beatitudes, and it raises priestly and religious vocations. To achieve these effects, firm doctrine is required, but overall, kindness of heart! So, clothe yourselves with the same sentiments of Jesus and proclaim to everybody what the author of the letter to the Hebrews wrote: Let us confidently approach the throne of grace to receive mercy and to find grace for timely help (Heb 4:16).
In ages past, the missions revolved around two main elements: the sermons and confessions. Nowadays another is added: the visit to families.

The missionary’s sermons are useful yet when the pastor preaches every Sunday, in a way that even the more ignorant people could get fruits, since he is not speaking about things pertaining to them, or about the problems that his parishioners present to him, “by force of always hearing the same voice, one ends up not being impressed with what hears.”
f: Saint Alphonsus Marie og Liguori, Letter to a new bishop, p.384.

t: One of the reasons for the massive attendance to the missions is that new voices, which speak simply and popularly, are heard, together with the explication of the eternal truths which are more effective for moving hearts, such as the importance of eternal salvation, the malice of sin, death, judgment, hell, eternity…,etc.

They are not few who, after having spent many years without confessing or after making a bad confession, finally during the Mission make a confession with a good disposition. It is the main fruit of the Missions. Many sacrilegious confessions, which are made keeping their sins in silent because of shame, are remedied. Now, they know that there are many foreign priests whom they do not know and who soon will be gone, people decide to vomit all their sins, which they had kept in secret for a long time.
For that reason the Mission should last the enough time in each place so that all the parishioners could have their confessions heard by the missionaries.

Nowadays, it does not suffice to call the sheepfold, but it is necessary to go and look for the sheep. Each missionary is able to say, as John Paul II did when he visited the Saint Francis Roman church in Rome: “Today, I come to your church [to your house] to carry out the principle apostolic ministry: the ministry of the visit.”
f: John Paul II, in the visit to the Saint Francis Roman Church, (29/11/1981).

t: Each family from our parishes should remember: Do not reject Christ who passes by in the person of the missionary! Saint Alphonsus affirms: “I am certain that  for those who have gone to the sermons of the mission, if one  dies within the year, with difficulty would he be condemned.”
f: Saint Alphonsus Marie of Liguori, op.cit.,  p. 390.

t: Saint Alphonsus refutes the main objections. In the first place: “...that the fruit of the missions turns into smoke, which seems great but, however, is of short duration, since, after the mission, sinners behave worse than before.” I answer: I hope all those who are converted persevere until death! Human misery makes many sinners lose the grace that they had recovered. But, even if there were no other advantages, it is certain that bad customs and scandals disappear during the mission, blasphemies cease, much restitution is made, and many bad confessions are repaired. Moreover, it is not true that all sinners behave worse after the mission than before; many of them persevere in God’s grace, and if some of them relapse, they are conserved far from mortal sin during many months; at least, due to the sermons heard in the mission, they acquire greater knowledge of God and of the importance of salvation, and a greater horror of sin, so that luckily, if they relapse, they will rise again before the paschal fulfillment. I am certain that for those who have gone to the sermons of the mission, if one dies within a year, with difficulty would he be condemned. The fruit of the Mission can be seen to last for at least one or two years after it, and if it doesn’t, it would be the fault of the priests of the place that do not make an effort to conserve the fruit of the mission with instructions, taking care to meet with the people to make a meditation and a visit to the Blessed Sacrament, and overall, being faithful to confessions. Sometimes, a year after the Mission, there are few fruits, but why? Because of the negligence of the priests who do not want to be bothered.”

In the second place: “ …the parish priest says missions disturb consciences due to the numerous scruples caused by the sermons…Would this priest want sinners to sleep in the lethargy of vice, in the bosom of that damned peace, which is the stamp of their condemnation? Would that the consciences be disturbed! What the devil wants is that the false peace of his unfortunate slaves, who live in a state of perdition, be not disturbed.”

In the third place: “… that the mission events finish at night, so it gives cause for many scandals. I answer that full fantasy is needed to claim that many sins are committed during the mission because it is preached at night.
